One connected front apron with its side rims, storage cup and locating bridges. It catches the marble at the player’s end.
The side rails, curved return lips and launch divider are fitted. The connected catch apron still belongs at the front.
A numbered wheel already retained on its bearing and edge rail. The rail clips to the table; turn the wheel by hand after a successful shot.
The three arches are in place. The manual score wheel clips onto the left edge.
A mirrored pair of light wings, each with a prepared hinge hole and its integral drive tab. One wing represents the pair.
One decorative card tail with its captive pin, washer and broad retainer. Its hole matches the prepared body hole.
The pins and spacing collars are fitted to the wings. Release and reseat their retainers when fitting the pair through the body’s shoulder holes.
Both wings pivot clear of the body. Fit the tail through its prepared hole before mounting the dragon.
One connected pair of C-shaped jaws on a bridge and central support. It fits the sliding crosshead and captures the output syringe’s thumb pad.
The capture clip is on the crosshead. Seat the syringe cups on the beam with its nozzle toward the handle, and snap its thumb pad into the clip.
Two strapped cups on prepared peel-and-stick feet, one shaped for the handgrip and the other for the beam. One complete holder represents the pair.
The strapped holders support the hand syringe beside the grip. Route the tube into its two gentle clips, keeping a free handling loop.
One measured insulated lead with its two inline connectors. It bridges the extended gap between the original controller lead and tile lead without stretching either.
Two rigid U-shaped fork saddles. Each has two legs and one crosshead. Their crossheads bear against the whale’s upper spar while their feet receive the lift cradle.
Two prepared straps, each one continuous piece. They retain the original upper cradle against the fork saddles after the module is seated.
One pushrod guide with its support flange and real rib bracket. It mounts beside the hatch, ready to receive the connected red button and pushrod.
The original supports retain their lengths; the four extra struts bridge the gap to the lower frame. The original short electrical leads need the measured extension before the module can run.
The added lead joins both original connectors. The complete module is still supported and disconnected while Jo helps seat it beneath the fork saddles.
The tile cradle meets the forks beneath the upper spar; the battery and counterweight hang low. Jo keeps the assembly supported while you fit the retaining straps.
The guide is mounted beside the hatch. Its open bore lines up the pushrod with the module’s stop switch.
Two connected crossbars, each with its guide rings and removable cradle-frame clamps. Fit them to the lower cradle before sliding their rings over the four posts.
Four broad retaining nuts. Fit them after the cradle is on the posts; the guide rings can travel below them without lifting off.
The two crossbars clamp to the lower cradle. Their open rings will slide over the stand’s bare posts.
The guide rings have slid over the four posts. Add the four retaining nuts before the first powered test.
A small teal parking plate on a short support arm. It mounts under the deck to hold the wired accessory switch.
The switch parking dock is fixed beneath the deck; the battery and fused power divider are not yet fitted.
